assets.doc:
WP2 assets, materials and Fab on a real editor. It writes its own source files on the box (an OBJ box the size of
a chair, a glTF cube, three PNG maps of a texture set), then: imports them (Interchange, no dialog), reads them back
(assets.describe, the registry catalog, assets.find "chair 90 cm tall"), sets mesh build settings (Nanite, LODs,
collision), textures by role, re-imports a changed file; builds all 12 library masters and checks each compiles and
that every texture matches its sampler; PBR from the set, presets, a graph material, instances that converge;
assigns a material to a mesh slot; renames, moves, duplicates, tags, follows references, fixes a redirector,
audits, removes; takes thumbnails; and checks Fab's state (the library only when signed in; fab.add needs a signed
URL and is not run). Takes ~3 min (12 master compiles on a cold DDC, 2 stills). Needs: GPU (stills, shader
statistics); Fab sign-in optional.

mh.doc:
WP3 MetaHuman creation, end to end on the box. Part 1 (no cloud): presets, a character from a preset and a blank one,
body measurements (constraint copies, range warnings, idempotent), face blend of two presets and a landmark move
(applied once), skin/freckles/texture resolution, eyes, eyelashes, teeth, makeup, the hair groom with melanin and
redness and its instance parameters, slots, describe/export, a variant copy, actionable errors, the live preview actor
and a still of it, mh.apply on a spec twice (second run changes nothing), a cast of 4 extras (mh.variants: distinct, same seed same
cast, previews in a row, a contact sheet through view.sheet). Part 2 (only with the Epic sign-in, else
noted and skipped): the cloud rig (multi-tick, ~30 s) and its up-to-date skip, the textures (~20 s), the cinematic
build (~3 min on an L4, the editor blocks), the built Blueprint placed, a garment of its own dressed on it with leader
pose (checked on the bones), a prop riding a bone, the clipping check, stills. Takes ~2 min without the cloud, ~6 min
with it. Needs: the MetaHuman Creator core data (presets); GPU for the stills; the Epic sign-in for part 2
(film-ue epic-login once per box).

render.doc: WP9's acceptance test: every render op on a scratch scene, on the GPU box, with numbers and frames to look at.

cam.doc: WP7's acceptance test: cameras and shooting, measured on real renders.

env.doc:
WP5's selftest: environments and lighting by spec, measured. Takes ~4 min on the L4 (scene captures and a few
stills; the reflection-capture rebuild runs a lighting build). Needs: GPU (a real RHI; offscreen is fine). No Epic
sign-in, no project assets: engine basic shapes and a material it makes in its scratch folder.

anim.doc: WP4's acceptance test: animation and performance, measured in the editor.

qa.doc:
WP10's selftest: Claude's eyes work in the real editor. Takes ~2 min on the L4 (most of it scene-capture warm-up
and the sequence review). Needs: GPU (a real RHI; offscreen is fine). No Epic sign-in, no project assets: the scene
is engine basic shapes. A MetaHuman part runs only when one is found under /Game/MetaHumans.

seq.doc:
WP8's acceptance test, the Sequencer core on a real editor: a scratch scene (a cube, a skeletal actor, two cine
cameras, a point light), a SEQUENCE SPEC applied over it with every track kind the core writes (transform with
look-at, visibility, skeletal animation, float / colour properties on components, a material parameter, camera cuts,
audio, fade, a parameter collection when one exists, markers), then:
